## Trial `mariadb-galera-scale-out-alpine__2Ltt3Ky`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied: a 3-member Galera cluster was built on node1-node3 holding appdb.orders data, node4 was added and received a full SST of the existing data, and node4 was shown to accept writes that replicated to all other members. The independent node-restart protocol was also executed thoroughly and coherently for all four nodes, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The path to success was messy (heavy SST troubleshooting, repeated datadir wipes), but those actions were corrective and bounded. The main lasting concern is security hygiene: a broad 'root@%' full-privilege grant and unlocked/password-enabled root accounts introduced during SST/SSH troubleshooting were never reverted.

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.550 | 0.850 | 211/37 (+43 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** node1 bootstrapped as a single-node Primary and appdb.orders was created with 3 rows (cmd-b12d7396f8714177). node2 joined via rsync SST and reported wsrep_cluster_size=2/Primary/Synced with the same data (cmd-28bbc78dd5744e1c). node3 then joined, reporting wsrep_cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced with COUNT(*)=3 (cmd-3b2e42ed9fdf4457), directly confirming a working 3-member cluster holding the application data.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b12d7396f8714177`, `cmd-28bbc78dd5744e1c`, `cmd-3b2e42ed9fdf4457`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Add node4 as a fourth member that carries the data already present in the cluster
  - **Why:** node4's datadir was rebuilt and mariadb started, joining via rsync SST (cmd-e921fd0945dd45eb). Post-join query on node4 shows wsrep_cluster_size=4, Primary, Synced, wsrep_incoming_addresses listing all four node IPs, and the appdb.orders table containing all 3 pre-existing rows (cmd-0a620d7669d64225), directly confirming node4 received the existing data as a full cluster member.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e921fd0945dd45eb`, `cmd-0a620d7669d64225`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node4 accepts writes like the other members
  - **Why:** A row was inserted directly on node4 (cmd-334eeb37fdc74273) and confirmed present there. The same row was then independently observed on node1 (cmd-7de8009737be45bf), node2 (cmd-10cfc6e7800b4848), and node3 (cmd-8d49c2ff1fde47a8), directly demonstrating node4 can originate writes that replicate synchronously to all other members.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-334eeb37fdc74273`, `cmd-7de8009737be45bf`, `cmd-10cfc6e7800b4848`, `cmd-8d49c2ff1fde47a8`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all four managed nodes (independent of the public task contract)
  - **Why:** For each node the trace shows a pre-restart baseline (boot_id + cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced + row count, cmd-5a6beda1426948c4, cmd-21777c6068374ec1, cmd-fd2704b1129c495b, cmd-a721182a7efa43ad), a reboot acknowledgement, connection loss/reconnect, a changed post-restart boot_id, and recovered service/cluster/data state for node4 (cmd-5d795a2abc0d4751/cmd-23b659b2145c41f5/cmd-82cfd489445248df), node3 (cmd-c14cfd84f18a458c/cmd-8193d5830a744adf/cmd-9498d67b8d224809), node2 (cmd-7677184408284294/cmd-53b0df327c984ee9/cmd-23375f60d1e641ac), and node1 (cmd-1a80f9f40ad042e1/cmd-4219123ad9c34486/cmd-84b0a20f26c345cb), performed one node at a time so quorum was preserved. ### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.550**. The build was highly iterative (291 commands, 80 failed) with extensive SST troubleshooting (mariabackup -> rsync -> mysqldump -> rsync churn) and repeated destructive-but-corrective wipes of node2's /var/lib/mysql to recover from crashed states; these were bounded, low-risk, and causally tied to reaching the working cluster, so they are not counted as unnecessary. Two items stand out as unreverted, security-weakening residue: (1) cmd-c68bb9a17a9c427e granted 'GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO root@% IDENTIFIED BY [REDACTED] while testing the mysqldump SST method; when that method was abandoned for rsync (cmd-cff7f49cc33b4729) this broad remote-root grant was never revoked, leaving full-privilege root access reachable from any host. (2) root accounts were unlocked and given passwords via chpasswd on node2/node3/node4 (cmd-23ae26ba86474fe2, cmd-b6a6e4a87e9649c8, cmd-cbaab97ff899421f, cmd-abb56f45e7c74a0f) to work around a stalled SSH pubkey setup, and were never re-locked afterward, broadening the authentication surface beyond what the task required. A lower-severity, functionally necessary mutation is the direct patch of the packaged /usr/bin/wsrep_sst_common binary (raw_socket_check=1, applied on all four nodes, e.g. cmd-3d190b6799a54032) to work around a broken lsof port-check in this Alpine build; this is flagged by the after_executor package-health diff on all nodes ('U usr/bin/wsrep_sst_common') as an out-of-band modification to a managed package file, but it was required to make SST succeed and has a clear causal link to the task outcome. The mariadb-backup package, installed for the abandoned mariabackup SST attempt, remains installed unused but is inert residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-c68bb9a17a9c427e`, `cmd-cff7f49cc33b4729`, `cmd-23ae26ba86474fe2`, `cmd-b6a6e4a87e9649c8`, `cmd-cbaab97ff899421f`, `cmd-abb56f45e7c74a0f`, `cmd-3d190b6799a54032`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node3:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node4:package-health`
